title: Ordinary decoding value bound
statement: Let $G$ be a regular unique game with label set $ in q$, where $q>0$, and let each vertex be assigned a function on the Boolean cube taking values in $[-1,1]$. For any threshold $	ext{ε}$ and default label, the expected edge agreement obtained by choosing uniformly from each vertex’s ordinary decoding candidates (using the default when a candidate set is empty) is at most the optimum value of the associated constraint satisfaction instance.
hypotheses_covered: The label set $ in q$ is nonempty ($q>0$)
A bounded cube function is given at every vertex
A real threshold ε is given
A default label in $ in q$ is given
